blocks.text: Imagine trying to build a complex network without any structure. Layered models provide the blueprint that makes this task manageable.

blocks.markdown: In computer networks, layered models are used to organize and standardize the functions of a network. By dividing network communication into layers, each with specific responsibilities, we can simplify design, implementation, and troubleshooting. Two primary models exist: the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model and the TCP/IP model.

blocks.title: Layered Model
blocks.text: A framework that divides network communication into a series of layers, each responsible for specific functions, to standardize and simplify the design and implementation of networks.

blocks.markdown: The OSI model is a conceptual framework used to understand and implement network protocols in seven layers. Each layer serves a specific function and communicates with the layers directly above and below it.

blocks.caption: Comparison of OSI and TCP/IP models

blocks.markdown: The TCP/IP model, also known as the Internet model, is a more simplified model with four layers. It was developed by the Department of Defense (DoD) to ensure robust, end-to-end data communication.

blocks.title: Layering Benefits
blocks.text: Layering allows for modularity, making it easier to update or replace parts of the network without affecting the entire system.

blocks.title: Mapping OSI to TCP/IP Layers
blocks.prompt: Map the OSI layers to their TCP/IP counterparts.

steps.text: Identify the OSI layers: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical.
Group the OSI Application, Presentation, and Session layers into the TCP/IP Application layer.
Map the OSI Transport layer to the TCP/IP Transport layer.
Map the OSI Network layer to the TCP/IP Internet layer.
Combine the OSI Data Link and Physical layers into the TCP/IP Link layer.

blocks.answer: The OSI Application, Presentation, and Session layers map to the TCP/IP Application layer; the OSI Transport layer maps to the TCP/IP Transport layer; the OSI Network layer maps to the TCP/IP Internet layer; and the OSI Data Link and Physical layers map to the TCP/IP Link layer.

blocks.markdown: Layering makes networks easier to evolve. By isolating functions into layers, changes in one layer don't require changes in others. This modularity allows for innovation and adaptation to new technologies.

blocks.title: Understanding Layer Functions
blocks.prompt: Explain the function of the Transport layer in the TCP/IP model.

steps.text: The Transport layer is responsible for end-to-end communication between devices.
It provides services such as connection-oriented communication, reliability, flow control, and error correction.

blocks.answer: The Transport layer ensures reliable or unreliable delivery of data between devices, providing services like connection management, flow control, and error correction.

points: The OSI model has seven layers, while the TCP/IP model has four layers.
Layering provides modularity, simplifying network design and evolution.
Each layer in the models has specific functions and communicates with adjacent layers.
